COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPMS No. 3036 of 2023
Hon 'b le Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.
(1) Mr. Vinay Kum ar, learned counsel
for the petitioner.
(2) Mr. Devendra Pant, learned Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.

(3) Petitioner is regularly appointed as
Medical Officer in Departm ent of Medical
Health & Family Welfare. According to
her, she was appointed as such in the
m onth of April, 2015. Petitioner was
desirous of pursuing postgraduate course
in Medical Science, therefore, she
applied for 'No Objection Certificate' from
her em ployer. No Objection Certificate
was given to petitioner on 02.03.2023,
but with the condition that it is valid for
clinical subjects only and not for
postgraduate courses in physiology,
biochemistry, pharm acology and
anatom y.
(4) I t is an admitted position that
petitioner took admission in
postgraduate course in Biochemistry in
Grant Medical College, Mum bai in 2023
and presently she is pursuing the said
course. From the NOC, issued on
02.03.2023, it is revealed that NOC is
not valid for postgraduate course in
Biochemistry. Petitioner has challenged
the condition im posed by State
Government in NOC dated 02.03.2023,
as arbitrary and discriminatory.

(5) Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that postgraduate m edical
courses cannot be classified into clinical
and non-clinical for the purpose of NOC.
(6) Learned State Counsel, however,
submits that there is acute shortage of
Medical Officers in Governm ent Hospitals
within the State, especially those situate
in rem ote hill/ rural areas. He further
submits that if Medical Officers are
indiscriminately given NOC for pursuing
postgraduate courses, regardless of
usefulness of such courses to the general
public of Uttarakhand, it will be very
difficult to run the Government
Hospitals, especially in hill/ rural areas.
He further submits that a Medical Officer,
upon com pletion of postgraduate course
in clinical subjects becomes an asset for
the Departm ent, as he is then better
equipped to serve the m asses. He
submits that Master degree in Surgery,
Cardiology, Neurology, Orthopaedic,
Paediatrics, Gynaecology etc. im proves
the worth of a Medical Officer, while
serving in Hospitals, while that is not the
case with Medical Officers with Masters
Degree in Anatom y, Biochemistry,
Pharm acology, Physiology etc. which are
relevant only for faculty positions in
Medical Colleges and not Hospitals. He
thus submits that State Government has
taken a considered policy decision to
grant NOC to Medical Officers, only for
pursuing Masters Course in clinical
subjects, which add to the value of such
Medical Officers for treating patients.
(7) Objection to the interim relief
application has been filed by Dr. Vinita
Shah, Director General, Medical Health &

Fam ily Welfare, Dehradun. Para 6 & 10
of the said objection are reproduced
below: -
"6 . That the study leave Government Order
dated 18.01.2021 in para 1 State as follows: -

1 0 . That the study leave is given for the
subjects which are relevant and beneficial for
the work conducted by the petitioners as
medical officer and beneficial for the patients
treated by them but Biochemistry being a non
clinical subject is of no value for the
department and for the work conducted by
the petitioner. Moreover, there is no such
post in the department after specialization of
Biochemistry by the petitioner."
(8) Thus, the stand taken by the
respondents is that Biochemistry is a
non-clinical subject which do not add any
value to a Medical Officer for rendering
service in the Departm ent of Medical
Health, moreover, there is no post
available in the Departm ent for a person
having M.D. Biochemistry Degree.

(9) From the objection filed by Director
General, it is revealed that State
Government has taken a considered
policy decision, in view of peculiar
problem s being faced in State of
Uttarakhand. I t is not the case of
petitioner that the said policy decision is
contrary to any Statutory provision.
(10) Law is well settled that State is free
to form ulate a policy and validity of a
policy can be challenged only when it is
in contravention of any Statutory
provision or it is in violation of som e
provision contained in the Constitution.
This is not the case here.
(11) Learned counsel for the petitioner
has relied upon Rule 146-A of Financial
Hand Book, which reads as under: -
"1 4 6 - A. The following rules have been made
by the Governor to regulate the grant of
additional leave to government servants for
the study of scientific, technical or similar
problems, or in order to undertake special
courses of instruction. These rules relate to
study leave only. They are not intended to
meet the case of government servants
deputed to other countries at the instance of
the Government, either for the performance of
special duties imposed on them or for the
investigation of specific problems connected
with their technical duties. Such cases will
continue to be dealt with on their merits under
the provisions of rules 50 and 51 of the Uttar
Pradesh Fundamental Rules. These rules apply
to the Public Health and Medical Research
Departments, the Civil Veterinary Department,
the Agricultural Department, the Education
Department, the Public Works Departm ent and
the Forest Department (except in respect of
Continental tours, to which special rules
apply). The rules may be extended by the
Government to any government servant not
belonging to any of the departments

mentioned above in whose case they may be
of opinion that leave should be granted in the
public interests to pursue a special course of
study or investigation of a scientific or
technical nature."
(12) The said Rule does not support the
contention of petitioner. Since petitioner
wants to pursue higher studies in a
subject which is of no use for the
Departm ent of Medical Health & Family
Welfare, therefore, em ployer i.e. State
Government cannot be com pelled to
grant NOC to petitioner for pursuing
further studies in a non-clinical course
like Biochemistry.
(13) I n view of the above discussion,
there is no scope for interference with
the impugned order. The writ petition
fails and is dismissed.

( Man oj Ku m ar Tiw ar i, J.)
